lead: Cellular generations are a short history of one idea: each generation adds one new capability to the mobile network. 1G carried analog voice. 2G made voice digital and added SMS. 2.5G added packet data. 3G raised data rates. 4G moved user traffic to IP packets. 5G targets high speed, low delay and network slicing. Mobile app developers care because the network under the app changes what the app may assume: always-on data, latency, and cost per megabyte. The figure places the main standards on a timeline.
prereq: You need: Chapter 1.1 for the device, link and fixed network picture.

sections.h3: 1G analog voice, 2G digital voice and SMS

blocks.text: The first generation (1G) sent voice as an analog radio signal. AMPS (Advanced Mobile Phone System) started in the United States in 1983. NMT (Nordic Mobile Telephone) started earlier in Northern Europe. Each call took one frequency channel. There was no native data service; a modem over the voice channel was the only option.

The second generation (2G) encoded voice as bits before transmission. GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) began in Europe in 1991. IS-95 cdmaOne was the main 2G standard in North America and parts of Asia. Digital voice gave more calls per band, encryption, and cheaper handsets.

SMS (Short Message Service) came with GSM as a use of the signalling channel. A short text message did not need a call to be set up. Typical 2G circuit data ran at an order of 10 kbps (kilobits per second), for example 9.6 kbps. That is enough for text, not for images or music.

GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) added packet switching to GSM. A phone could stay online and pay for the bytes it sent, not for the time it held a circuit. GPRS data rates are an order of 100 kbps; the common textbook peak is 171.2 kbps. EDGE improved the modulation and reached an order of 200 kbps. Operators marketed both as 2.5G.

3G introduced a new radio interface. UMTS (Universal Mobile Telecommunications System) uses WCDMA (Wideband Code Division Multiple Access). CDMA2000 is the other main 3G family. 3G data rates are an order of 2 Mbps at peak and often 384 kbps in practice. That made mobile video calling and early mobile web usable. HSDPA is a 3.5G downlink upgrade inside UMTS, with rates an order of 10 Mbps. The internal GSM, GPRS and UMTS architecture is in Chapter 1.3.

blocks.where: T is the download time in seconds; S is the file size in bits; R is the data rate in bits per second.

blocks.text: 4G LTE (Long Term Evolution) dropped circuit switching for user traffic. Voice, SMS and web all travel as IP packets; VoLTE carries voice over the same packet network. LTE uses OFDMA (Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access) on the downlink: many narrow subcarriers are shared among users. 4G rates are an order of 100 Mbps. The ITU IMT-Advanced target was 100 Mbps for a moving user and 1 Gbps for a slow user.

5G NR (New Radio) is the 5G air interface. It uses wider channels, including mmWave bands above 24 GHz, and massive antenna arrays. 5G rates are an order of 1 Gbps. It also targets low latency, about 1 ms in the radio link for some services. Network slicing divides one physical network into virtual networks, each with its own speed, latency and capacity guarantee. A factory robot slice can differ from a video streaming slice.

sections.h3: Satellite and terrestrial broadcast as other paths

blocks.text: A mobile user can also receive data without a cellular tower. Satellite systems cover oceans and rural areas. GEO satellites sit at about 35,786 km and add about 250 ms one-way delay; LEO constellations are lower and faster but need many satellites. A satellite link is shared and costly per megabyte.

Terrestrial broadcast systems send one signal from a tall tower to many receivers. FM radio, digital audio broadcast and DVB-T television are examples. Broadcast is cheap for popular content because the cost does not grow with each viewer. It is mostly downlink: the user needs another path for requests.

figure.caption: One 40 Mbit song on three networks: 4167 s (69.4 min) on 2G, 104.2 s (1.7 min) on 3G, and 2.0 s on 4G. The oldest generation makes you wait longest.

spec.aria: A tree shows one 40 Mbit song file split into three download paths: 2G at 9.6 kbps taking 4167 seconds, 3G at 384 kbps taking 104.2 seconds, and 4G at 20 Mbps taking 2.0 seconds.

examples.question: A 5 MB song must be downloaded to a phone. Use 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes and 1 byte = 8 bits. Find the download time on 2G at 9.6 kbps, on 3G at 384 kbps, and on 4G at 20 Mbps. Give seconds, and minutes where useful.
steps: Convert the file size to bits: S = 5 × 8 × 10⁶ = 40,000,000 bit.
Convert the rates: 2G R = 9.6 kbps = 9,600 bps; 3G R = 384 kbps = 384,000 bps; 4G R = 20 Mbps = 20,000,000 bps.
examples.answer: About 4167 s (69.4 min) on 2G, 104.2 s (1.7 min) on 3G, and 2.0 s on 4G.
examples.check:
size = 5 * 8 * 10**6
t2 = size / 9600
t3 = size / 384000
t4 = size / 20000000
print(round(t2))
print(round(t2 / 60, 1))
print(round(t3, 1))
print(round(t3 / 60, 1))
print(round(t4, 1))

traps: GPRS is 2.5G, not 3G. 3G starts with UMTS/WCDMA or CDMA2000.
2.5G and 3.5G are upgrades inside the same system. They do not replace the air interface.
5 MB is 40 Mbit, not 5 Mbit. Convert bytes to bits before dividing by a rate in bits per second.
cdmaOne (IS-95) is 2G; CDMA2000 is 3G. The similar names are an easy slip.
A higher generation number does not promise a fixed speed. Rate depends on load, distance and spectrum.

quiz.q: Name the two main 2G digital standards mentioned in this chapter.
Which generation first carried voice as an analog radio signal?
Why did SMS arrive with 2G rather than 1G?
quiz.a: 2G sends voice and signalling as digital bits. GSM has a signalling channel that can carry a short text message without setting up a voice call.

quiz.q: Explain network slicing in one sentence.
quiz.a: Network slicing divides one physical 5G network into virtual networks, each with its own speed, latency and capacity guarantee for a service.

quiz.q: A 2 MB photo is 16 Mbit. Find its download time on 3G at 384 kbps.
Why is GPRS called 2.5G and not 3G?
quiz.a: GPRS adds packet data to the existing GSM air interface. It does not introduce a new 3G radio interface, and its rates are an order of 100 kbps, below 3G rates.

quiz.q: A remote village has no cellular coverage. Name two other delivery paths from this chapter and give one limitation of each.
quiz.a: Satellite: coverage is wide, but GEO latency is high and cost per megabyte is high. Terrestrial broadcast: cheap for many viewers, but it is mostly downlink, so requests need another path.

quiz.q: Order these generations from lowest to highest typical data rate: 4G, 2G, 5G, 3G.

beyond: Not for the exam. The standards work continues in 3GPP releases, with 5G-Advanced and research toward 6G. Non-terrestrial networks aim to connect satellites and cellular systems. Open RAN changes how operators build radio networks. Search next for 3GPP release timeline, ITU IMT-2020, and 5G network slicing.
